key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a proven worst-case bound of 5(n−1) rounds, matching the known Ω(n) lower bound up to constants.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens the theoretical runtime guarantees for graph refinement methods used in graph isomorphism, algebraic graph theory, and machine-learning pipelines.
method: Prove a new upper bound on stabilization rounds for the classical 2-WL algorithm.
Extend the argument to k-WL for every k≥3, yielding improved iteration bounds.
Generalize the proof to a broader class of tuple-coloring refinement sequences.
evidence_signal: The paper gives a theoretical worst-case analysis and improves the previous O(n log n) upper bound to 5(n−1), with corresponding improved bounds for k-WL.
watch_item: The bound is about number of refinement rounds, not total wall-clock cost, so practical implementation speed still depends on per-round work and graph size.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
